purpose: Layer model, material parameters, and reference board for the fourteen reviewed Liquid Glass icons.
copyrightBoundary: Apple artwork and screen captures are research-only evidence. Production PNGs are original layered constructions. No screenshot crop, extracted asset, or traced path ships as a runtime icon.

systemRules.authoring: Each object is a layer list plus a symbol drawing, never a flattened picture. The material stack is applied by the renderer from the parameters below, so one artwork serves every appearance instead of three separate drawings.
systemRules.layerRule: Two or three simple bold layers: a background that carries the colour identity, one primary symbol layer, and an accent only when the function needs it. Layer count is never raised to create more refraction.
systemRules.enclosure: Application objects sit in the system rounded-square enclosure with the measured corner geometry. Finder objects that are free-form in the real system stay free-form: folder, document, trash, and volumes keep their own silhouettes.
systemRules.material: Background glass carries colour and low transparency. Foreground glass is clearer, has a brighter specular edge, and refracts the background it covers. Detail layers refract least. The three tiers never share one parameter set.
systemRules.refraction: The foreground layer redraws the background it covers, displaced and lightened, so the glass changes what passes through it. Transparency alone is not refraction and does not count as Liquid Glass.
systemRules.specular: Directional: a bright top and upper-left rim that fades along the lower edge, plus one inner highlight on the foreground layer. A uniform white border around every edge is forbidden.
systemRules.shadow: Soft and ambient, separating glass layers and floating the object. It is not a Snow Leopard object shadow and it is not a shared CSS drop-shadow.
systemRules.smallArt: Runtime surfaces downsample the reviewed 128 px Default asset. The 64/32/16 and Dark/Clear files are deterministic Theme Lab review derivatives with a contrast hint, not separately authored artwork.
systemRules.toolbarBoundary: Toolbar and sidebar symbols are a separate small family. A 128 px application icon is never scaled down to stand in for one.
systemRules.grid: Every object is placed on the shared icon grid in tooling/lib/icon-grid.mjs: one live dimension per shape class (square, portrait, landscape) with a margin that no object may cross, plus small optical allowances for shapes that read large or small at equal bounds. Objects are scaled uniformly, never stretched, so a row reads as one family while each object keeps its own proportions.

continuityRule: System objects follow the real Tahoe 26 prototype. The seven AI System 6 objects keep the metaphorKey recorded in assets/themes/icon-system-continuity.json, rebuilt as bold layered shapes rather than the Yosemite artwork placed inside a glass tile.

default.note: Full colour identity on a light desktop.

dark.note: Deepened identity colour, dimmer glass, brighter rim, and raised symbol contrast. It is not a brightness filter over the default render.

clear.note: Colour drops to a faint tint while silhouette, layering, specular, and refraction carry the icon. The symbol keeps a dark core with a light halo so it stays readable on both light and dark desktops. It is not opacity applied to the default render.

captures.kind: macOS Tahoe 26 screen captures, including the four appearance styles, the desktop and Dock, and Finder
captures.use: Enclosure geometry, Dock scale, folder and trash treatment, and how the system states Default, Dark, Clear Light, Clear Dark, and Tinted.
captures.redistribution: Copyrighted screenshots; local research and comparison only.

iconComparisons.kind: Side-by-side macOS 15 and macOS 26 application icons
iconComparisons.use: The controlling evidence for what changed: layer separation, rim light, translucency of the foreground shape, and the deeper colour ramp.

wallpapers.use: Background material tests. A Liquid Glass icon that only works on a white page is not finished.

sessions.kind: WWDC session transcripts on the icon system and Icon Composer
sessions.use: Layer model, appearance variants, and the stated design direction of simple bold layers.

referenceBoard.label: Finder
referenceBoard.observation: The pale half is no longer a flat colour split. It is a separate inset glass panel with its own rounded silhouette, a bright edge, and the blue showing through its lower part.

referenceBoard.label: Generic folder
layers: inset white symbol when the folder has a role
referenceBoard.observation: Folders stay free-form and saturated, with a thin bright rim and a monochrome inset symbol. Tahoe also personalises folder colour and symbol, so a role folder is the folder plus a symbol, never a new silhouette.

referenceBoard.label: Trash
referenceBoard.observation: Trash is free-form and mostly clear glass: the wallpaper reads through it and the ribs are specular lines rather than drawn wire.

referenceBoard.label: Document
referenceBoard.observation: Documents stay free-form paper, brighter and simpler than 10.10, with a soft floating shadow instead of a keyline.

referenceBoard.label: Dock family
referenceBoard.observation: Every application shares one enclosure shape and one specular treatment while keeping its own colour identity and symbol. Uniform container, never uniform content.

referenceBoard.label: Appearance styles
referenceBoard.observation: Clear keeps silhouette, layering, and specular while dropping colour. Dark rebalances the background and raises symbol contrast. Neither is the default render with a filter over it.

referenceBoard.label: Settings
referenceBoard.observation: The gear survives from 10.6 and 10.10 but becomes one bold monochrome layer instead of a modelled steel object.
